output.summary: An aquatic perennial native to northern and eastern Australia, and possibly New Guinea, the blue waterlily has large floating leaves and blue or lilac flowers that fade almost white. After fertilisation, its fruit is drawn underwater to ripen. Indigenous Australians traditionally ate roasted tubers, raw peeled stalks and flower buds, and roasted seeds or seed flour.
output.edibilityNote: Indigenous Australians ate roasted tubers, raw peeled stalks and flower buds, and seeds roasted or pounded into flour.
